charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Experian plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Experian plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date. Experian itself targets leverage on a Net Debt / Benchmark EBITDA basis (1.7x in FY2026, see KPI card) inside its 1.75x-2.0x target range -- watch this ratio, not the absolute debt level, for covenant and capital-allocation signal.

What to watch:

  • Net debt / EBITDA trend versus the 1.75x-2.0x target range
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Experian plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Experian plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested. Experian itself quotes Benchmark EPS (a decade of history: $0.891 FY2016 to $1.798 FY2026, see KPI card) which strips acquisition amortisation and other adjustments the statutory EPS plotted here still carries -- it is the figure management and sell-side analysts actually track.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt
  • Statutory EPS tracking well below Benchmark EPS (adjustment creep)

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Experian plc: Experian separately reports a non-GAAP Benchmark free cash flow (US$1,600m FY2026, see KPI card) that is close to, but not identical to, the statutory FreeCashFlow column plotted here -- the DCF's own reported_fcf input is anchored to that Benchmark figure.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF
  • Benchmark FCF vs statutory FCF converging or diverging

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Experian plc: these are statutory margins. Experian's own headline KPI is Benchmark EBIT margin (28.6% in FY2026, per the KPI card above) -- it excludes acquisition amortisation, M&A costs and other one-offs the statutory operating margin (23.8% FY2025) still carries, so expect Benchmark margin to run a few points above the statutory line.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • The gap between statutory and Benchmark EBIT margin widening (a sign of growing adjustments)

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Experian plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed. Experian's own disclosure frames this as CapEx at 8.6% of revenue (FY2026) and reports ROCE of 17.2% (FY2026, see KPI cards) as the return earned on the capital this spending builds.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue, or CapEx % of revenue drifting above its ~8.5-9% range
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA
  • ROCE trend versus the cost of capital

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Experian plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Experian plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Experian plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
